status_summary: Executive Order 14265 (signed 2025-04-09, published 2025-04-15) set a commercial-solutions-first preference and ordered a review of major programs more than 15 percent behind schedule or over cost for possible cancellation (no public result was found), and on 2025-05-01 the Army announced it would end procurement of the AH-64D, stop buying the HMMWV and JLTV, drop the Gray Eagle drone and move funding toward capability-based portfolios. A Secretary of War memorandum dated 2025-11-07 (read in the Internet Archive snapshot of the official copy) redesignated the acquisition system the Warfighting Acquisition System effective immediately and directed Portfolio Acquisition Executives (PAEs) built from existing program executive offices, with each component to submit within 60 days a plan moving all major acquisition into PAE portfolios within two years; its appendix sets 90-day commercial-first guidance, a 150-day update of the 5000-series instructions, the Financial Management Regulation and DFARS, and 180-day tasks on portfolio scorecards, options for a Warfighting Acquisition University and budget flexibility, including a PB 2027 PPBE reform package. The attached Acquisition Transformation Strategy states plans for PAE funding flexibility, PPBE Commission reforms, more multiyear procurement and a renamed Warfighting Acquisition University. The FY2026 NDAA (Public Law 119-60, 2025-12-18) lists sections on the portfolio acquisition executive role (Sec. 1802), commercial products and services (Sec. 1822), multiyear procurement authority (Sec. 804) and a Defense Acquisition University report (Sec. 825), which an industry guide describes as making the PAE a statutory senior acquisition official and expanding multiyear eligibility, and by March 2026 the Navy had set up six PAEs and was transitioning three more. For FY2027 the House passed H.R. 8800 216 to 212 on 2026-07-22 while cloture on the motion to proceed to S. 4784 failed 50 to 46 on 2026-07-14, and CRS showed no FY2027 authorization enacted as of 2026-09-01; the outputs of the memo's budget-flexibility and university tasks, any enacted PPBE change and revised Buy America treatment of defense items were not found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14265 (signed 2025-04-09, published 2025-04-15) prefers commercial and other streamlined buying pathways, orders reviews of major defense acquisition programs for possible cancellation and of the joint requirements process, and sets reform-plan deadlines of 60 to 180 days.

Army Secretary and Chief of Staff letter announces the Army Transformation Initiative: end of AH-64D procurement, excess HMMWV and JLTV, and the Gray Eagle drone, a shift from program-based to capability-based portfolios, and a merger of Futures Command and Training and Doctrine Command.

A Secretary of War memorandum dated 2025-11-07 redesignates the Defense Acquisition System the Warfighting Acquisition System effective immediately, with its provisions taking precedence over inconsistent policies. Its appendix directs Portfolio Acquisition Executives formed by reorganizing program executive offices, with components to nominate initial portfolios within 30 days and to submit within 60 days plans moving all major acquisition into PAE portfolios within two years; personnel policies within 60 days for PAE and program manager tenure of at least four years with two-year extensions; a Wartime Production Unit within 60 days; commercial-first guidance within 90 days; updates within 150 days to the 5000-series instructions, the Financial Management Regulation and DFARS; and, within 180 days, portfolio scorecards, options to turn Defense Acquisition University into a Warfighting Acquisition University, and budget-flexibility steps including a PB 2027 PPBE reform package. These are directed tasks, not reported outcomes.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of War (memorandum, read in the Internet Archive snapshot of 2025-12-23)

timeline.event: The Department posts its Acquisition Transformation Strategy (Rebuilding the Arsenal of Freedom; posted date from the media.defense.gov path). It plans to realign some program executive officers as PAEs with more authority over resources and requirements, to give PAEs more freedom to shift funds, to pursue 2024 PPBE Commission reforms, to seek more multiyear procurement from Congress, to reduce dependence on non-allied suppliers, and to rename Defense Acquisition University the Warfighting Acquisition University.
The Navy establishes its first PAE, for robotics and autonomous systems (December 2025; day not given, first of month used).

The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act becomes Public Law 119-60 (S. 1071; date shown on govinfo.gov). Its table of contents lists Sec. 1802 (portfolio acquisition executive), Sec. 1822 (commercial products and services), Sec. 804 (multiyear procurement authority) and Sec. 825 (Defense Acquisition University report); an industry guide published 2025-12-23 describes statutory PAEs, commercial solutions as the starting point, wider multiyear eligibility and a university effectiveness review.

The Navy announces five more PAEs (maritime, undersea, industrial operations, strategic systems, Marine Corps); PAEs take over contract, technical, and sustainment authority from the systems commands (March 2026; day not given, first of month used).

The House passes its FY2027 NDAA (H.R. 8800), 216 to 212 (roll call 278). A War on the Rocks comparison published 2026-07-16, before passage, reports that the House bill would let PAEs issue performance ratings and shift up to 10 percent of research funds to procurement, and that both bills extend multiyear procurement authority for munitions (13 in the House, 19 in the Senate). Cloture on the motion to proceed to the Senate bill (S. 4784) failed 50 to 46 on 2026-07-14; CRS shows neither bill enacted as of 2026-09-01.

uncertainties: The memorandum was read in the Internet Archive snapshot of 2025-12-23 of its media.defense.gov address (a 43-page PDF, 4,499,336 bytes); the official address still could not be opened in this review. The signature is an image and no signer's name appears in the text layer; the letterhead reads Secretary of War and the date stamp 2025-11-07. Page references come from the reading of that copy. The appendix passage directing the transition does not say from what date the two years run (plans are due within 60 days and must move all major acquisition into portfolios within two years); the phrase about 24 months appears only in the attached Strategy, describing the lack of a pathway to deliver kill chains within 24 months, and is not a deadline. The memo directs tasks and sets deadlines; whether the 30-day implementing guidance, the Military Department plans, the 60-day personnel policies (four-year minimum PAE and program manager tenure with two-year extensions), the Wartime Production Unit, the 150-day updates to the 5000-series instructions, the Financial Management Regulation and DFARS, the 180-day scorecards, the university options or the PB 2027 PPBE reform package were delivered was not found. The NDAA text itself was seen only through the table of contents on govinfo.gov (Public Law 119-60); the effect of Secs. 804, 825, 1802 and 1822 comes from an industry guide (War on the Rocks), and the page date 2025-12-18 is not labeled as the approval date. The table of contents shows no section on PPBE reform, block buys or a general Buy America change (Sec. 831 concerns the Berry Amendment and seafood only), but the body text was not searched. Not found: whether any program was cancelled through the EO 14265 review (the Army letter does not say), any PPBE reform in practice, or any outcome of the Defense Acquisition University tasks. Navy PAE events rest on Breaking Defense, and month-only events use first-of-month dates. The Acquisition Transformation Strategy on media.defense.gov was read through its first 100,000 of about 120,000 characters and states plans, not completed actions, including pursuit of those 2024 PPBE Commission reforms that provide resourcing flexibility; the Commission made 28 recommendations and the Strategy does not say how many will be adopted. FY2027 House provisions come from a War on the Rocks comparison published before House passage, not from bill text; House passage and the failed Senate cloture vote were confirmed on the House Clerk and Senate roll call pages. A vendor-hosted document once taken as a copy of the memo is a vendor-prepared summary; its four-year PAE terms correspond to the memo's direction to develop personnel policies with a four-year minimum PAE and program manager tenure.
